Lengthy negotiations. Benjamin Netanyahu remains prime minister of the caretaker government. A new election becomes possible.
How the result comes aboutAt the centre of the simulations, the Netanyahu camp holds 55.0 seats and the anti-Netanyahu camp 53.6. The two Arab lists total 11.3. They count towards no majority: the main lists of the anti-Netanyahu camp have ruled out governing with them. Yisrael Beytenu and Hendel-Zelekha refuse to govern with the ultra-Orthodox parties. The model assumes that Yashar will not govern with Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud. When the anti-Netanyahu camp reaches 61 seats, Yashar is its largest list in 84% of cases: Gadi Eisenkot would then be the natural candidate for prime minister.

Benjamin Netanyahu's camp won 64 seats. Yashar and Amcha Yisrael did not exist. Benny Gantz's National Unity has broken up: Blue and White runs alone, New Hope joined Likud and Gadi Eisenkot founded Yashar.

The electoral rules

A single nationwide constituency, 120 seats, election on Tuesday, October 27, 2026.
The threshold
A list needs 3.25% of valid votes to win seats, which means at least four.
The allocation
The 120 seats are allocated by national proportional representation, using the Bader-Ofer method, a variant of the D'Hondt method.
Surplus agreements
Two lists may pool their remainders for the last seat. Agreements must be filed by October 16.
Forming the government
The President consults the elected groups, then asks a member to form a government within 28 days, extendable by 14. If that fails, another member has 28 days, then a majority of members may put one forward. Otherwise the Knesset is dissolved and voters go back to the polls.
The Arab lists
The Central Elections Committee voted on September 23 to disqualify Ra'am and the Joint List. These decisions are being challenged before the Supreme Court, which has not yet ruled. Both cases are shown.

The test on past elections

The model replayed on the five elections from 2019 to 2022, 24 days before the vote, using only the polls then available. The tested election is removed from everything the model learns from the past. No setting was changed after this test.
ElectionNetanyahu camp at 61seats forecastseats wonmajority
April 201958%6265yes
September 201918%5755no
March 20201%5558no
March 2021< 1%4852no
November 202234%6064yes

The model rated the actual outcome as the most likely in 4 elections out of 5. Its Brier score, which measures the gap between stated probabilities and what happened, is 0.129; it would be 0.240 by always stating the average frequency of majorities. Lower is better.

How it works

A forecasting model is not one more poll. A poll surveys a sample and describes opinion at a given moment. A model surveys no one. It gathers what can be measured, published polls, past election results and the campaign context, and derives a distribution of possible outcomes with their probability. It does not say that a list will win 22 seats. It says within which range it will finish, and how likely each outcome is.

Why it is sturdier than a single poll

Two pollsters published on the same day can differ by several seats. The model aggregates every poll published since the lists were filed, giving more weight to the most recent, the largest and the pollsters that erred least in the past. It takes into account the last election, list by list, and the campaign context. When a source provides no reliable measurement, it does not count, and its share goes to the others.

Past polling errors

Israeli polls erred at each of the five elections from 2019 to 2022. The model replays these real errors on today's polls, in both directions: it does not assume in advance that a camp will be underestimated. This is what gives each list its range and each outcome its probability.

Seats, not just votes

Each simulation allocates the 120 seats under Israeli electoral law: 3.25% threshold, Bader-Ofer method and surplus agreements. Who governs is then read from the refusals to govern together that list leaders have stated publicly during the campaign.

No certainty on display

Uncertainty is this model's product, never its flaw. The computation is exact and reproducible, and the model was replayed on the five elections from 2019 to 2022 without any setting being changed afterwards.

Sources

Results: Central Elections Committee. Polls: pollsters and broadcasters, reports filed with the Committee's register. Past elections: public compilations of 2019 to 2022 polls. Statements by list leaders: Jerusalem Post, Times of Israel, Ynet, Israel National News.
